tasks.prompt: Order the annual management review cycle under the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one municipal system annual cycle from data gathering to top management decisions.

cards.label: Schedule the review and confirm top management, the owner representative, and operational leads will attend
Compile inputs including audit results, corrective actions, water quality trends, and infrastructure review findings
Circulate the input package in advance so participants can review evidence before the meeting
Hold the review meeting and assess whether the quality management system remains suitable and effective
Record decisions, assigned actions, owners, and due dates in the management review minutes
Track the assigned actions to completion and report progress at the next operational review

tasks.explanation: Management review needs evidence before judgment. Inputs are compiled and circulated first, the review itself makes the decisions, and tracked follow up proves the system improves rather than only meeting on paper.

tasks.prompt: Order the endorsement sequence for a revised DWQMS operational plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: revised operational plan from drafting to endorsed implementation.

cards.label: Confirm the current endorsed plan, the municipal drinking water licence, and the elements that must change
Draft the revisions with the quality management system representative and operational leads
Review the draft against every element of the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard for completeness
Obtain endorsement signatures from top management and communication to the owner as required
Communicate the endorsed plan to all staff whose work it affects and file superseded versions
Verify staff awareness and use of the new plan during the next internal audit

tasks.explanation: A plan cannot be endorsed before it is complete, and endorsement has no effect until staff are working from the new version. Verification in audit closes the loop.

tasks.prompt: Order the internal audit program sequence for a DWQMS system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one annual internal audit from program planning to reported findings.

cards.label: Set the audit scope, criteria, and schedule so every DWQMS element is audited within the required cycle
Assign trained auditors who are independent of the areas they will audit
Prepare checklists and notify the areas to be audited of dates and required records
Conduct the audit interviews, record reviews, and field observations and collect objective evidence
Classify findings, agree them with the audited areas, and issue the audit report
Enter nonconformities into the corrective action system with owners and due dates

tasks.explanation: Independence and preparation come before evidence gathering. Findings only become useful once they enter the corrective action system where they can be tracked.

tasks.prompt: Order the corrective action sequence after a DWQMS audit finds a nonconformity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one nonconformity from identification to verified closure.

cards.label: Describe the nonconformity clearly and cite the requirement and the objective evidence
Contain the immediate problem so drinking water quality and compliance are protected
Investigate the root cause with the staff who perform the work
Agree corrective actions that address the root cause, with owners and due dates
Implement the actions and update any affected procedures or training
Verify effectiveness after a suitable period and close the item only if the problem has not recurred

tasks.explanation: Containment protects water quality first, but closure requires root cause action and a later effectiveness check. Closing on paperwork alone leaves the cause in place.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual risk assessment review sequence for a drinking water system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: system wide review of hazards and hazardous events from source to consumer tap.

cards.label: Assemble the review team including operations, maintenance, water quality, and management staff
Review the existing hazard list against new source, process, and distribution information for the year
Assess each hazard for likelihood and consequence and identify existing control measures
Flag risks where controls are weak and rank them for action
Assign risk reduction actions and update the risk assessment document and operational plan references
Communicate the updated critical control points and limits to operating staff

tasks.explanation: The team must see the full hazard picture before ranking risks. Updated assessments only protect the system once operating staff know the revised control points.

tasks.prompt: Order the continual improvement planning sequence following management review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: turning management review outputs into a tracked improvement plan for the year.

cards.label: Collect improvement opportunities from audits, reviews, incident lessons, and staff suggestions
Screen the opportunities for water quality benefit, compliance risk, and feasibility
Select the priority improvements and define measurable success criteria for each one
Assign owners, resources, and completion dates in a written improvement plan
Implement the plan and monitor progress at scheduled operational meetings
Report results and lessons at the next management review and carry forward unfinished items

tasks.explanation: Selection and measurable criteria come before implementation. Reporting back to management review connects one improvement cycle to the next.

tasks.prompt: Order the infrastructure review sequence required to support DWQMS planning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual review of treatment and distribution infrastructure condition and needs.

cards.label: Compile condition, capacity, and performance information for treatment, storage, and distribution assets
Review recent failures, inspection findings, and maintenance history for each major asset group
Identify infrastructure that limits capacity, reliability, or water quality compliance
Prioritize renewal and upgrade needs by risk to service and compliance
Feed the priorities into the capital forecast and the management review input package
Record the review, its conclusions, and the decisions taken in the quality management system files

tasks.explanation: Evidence about condition and failures must precede prioritization. The review matters because its priorities flow into capital planning and management review.

tasks.prompt: Order the management of change sequence for a significant treatment process change.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one major change, a new chemical system, from proposal to steady operation.

cards.label: Describe the proposed change, its purpose, and the processes and documents it will affect
Assess risks to water quality, safety, and compliance and define controls for the transition
Obtain approval from the overall responsible operator and top management before work starts
Update procedures, drawings, training, and the operational plan before the change goes live
Implement the change under supervision with enhanced monitoring during the transition period
Review performance after the transition, confirm the change is stable, and close the change record

tasks.explanation: Approval, documentation, and training must be ready before the change goes live, not after. The post change review confirms the system actually absorbed the change.

tasks.prompt: Order the DWQMS policy review and communication sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual review of the quality management system policy and its communication to staff and the public.

cards.label: Review the current policy against system performance, audit results, and any changes in ownership or scope
Draft any revisions with the quality management system representative and top management
Obtain top management approval and endorsement of the revised policy
Communicate the policy to all staff and confirm understanding at team meetings
Make the policy available to the public and to suppliers as the standard requires
File the approved policy and keep evidence of communication for audit purposes

tasks.explanation: An approved policy that staff have never seen fails the standard in practice. Communication evidence is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought.

tasks.prompt: Order the readiness sequence for a DWQMS accreditation audit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing for an external accreditation audit of the quality management system.

cards.label: Confirm the audit scope, dates, and the standard version the auditors will use
Run a gap check of every element against the standard and fix documentation gaps found
Complete the internal audit and management review so both are current before the external visit
Brief staff on likely auditor questions and ensure records are retrievable within minutes
Host the audit, provide requested evidence, and record every finding raised
Enter external findings into the corrective action system and respond within the required timelines

tasks.explanation: External auditors test whether the internal system already works. Current internal audits and management review are therefore prerequisites, not optional extras.

tasks.prompt: Order the integrated management review sequence covering quality, safety, and assets together.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one combined annual review for the DWQMS, safety, and asset management systems.

cards.label: Set the combined agenda and the inputs required from each management system
Compile performance, audit, incident, and improvement data across all three systems
Review the inputs together to find conflicts, shared causes, and combined opportunities
Agree integrated decisions, priorities, and resource allocations for the coming year
Record the decisions and assign actions with owners and dates in one tracker
Report completion of the actions at the next integrated review and to the owner

tasks.explanation: Reviewing the systems together exposes shared causes that separate reviews miss. One action tracker prevents the same improvement being assigned three times.

tasks.prompt: Order the capital project initiation sequence for a treatment plant upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: from identified need to an approved project in the capital program.

cards.label: Document the need using condition, capacity, compliance, and risk evidence
Develop options at a conceptual level with whole life cost and risk comparisons
Select the preferred option and prepare the business case with scope, budget, and schedule
Obtain owner and senior management approval to add the project to the capital program
Assign a project manager and establish the project charter and governance
Release initial funding for design development and procurement planning

tasks.explanation: Need and options come before approval, and approval comes before spending on design. Skipping the business case leaves the project without a defensible scope or budget.

tasks.prompt: Order the design review leadership sequence for a treatment process upgrade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior review of consultant design from concept to issued for construction drawings.

cards.label: Confirm the design basis, rated capacity, water quality targets, and applicable Ontario requirements
Review the conceptual design with operations and maintenance staff for operability
Review detailed drawings and specifications and issue consolidated owner comments
Verify the designer has resolved comments and completed hazard and operability checks
Confirm the design includes commissioning, training, and spare parts requirements
Approve the design for tender only after operations sign off is recorded

tasks.explanation: Operations review must shape the design while changes are still cheap. Owner sign off before tender prevents building a plant that is hard to run.

tasks.prompt: Order the procurement evaluation sequence for a major equipment supply contract.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: competitive procurement of a major treatment equipment package.

cards.label: Finalize the specification, evaluation criteria, and weighted scoring before bids are invited
Issue the tender and respond to bidder questions through formal addenda only
Open bids as scheduled and check each bid for compliance with mandatory requirements
Score compliant bids with the evaluation team using the published criteria
Verify references, lifecycle costs, and delivery commitments for the leading bidder
Award the contract through the required approvals and notify all bidders of the result

tasks.explanation: Criteria fixed before bids arrive keep the evaluation fair and defensible. Award follows verification, and notification closes the process transparently.

tasks.prompt: Order the construction oversight sequence for work inside an operating treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: contractor construction alongside live treatment operations.

cards.label: Hold a pre construction meeting covering scope, schedule, site rules, and protection of water quality
Approve the contractor isolation, lockout, and disinfection plans before work in process areas
Inspect work at defined hold points and record deficiencies as they are found
Manage changes through written change orders with cost and schedule effects approved in advance
Verify completed sections meet specifications before they are covered or placed in service
Maintain a deficiency list and clear it progressively toward substantial completion

tasks.explanation: Water quality protection plans must be approved before construction touches the process. Hold point inspections prevent defects being buried and discovered at commissioning.

tasks.prompt: Order the commissioning leadership sequence for a new treatment train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new train from construction completion to operational acceptance.

cards.label: Confirm construction is complete, deficiencies are listed, and systems are safe to energize
Complete dry testing of equipment, valves, instruments, and control loops without process water
Introduce water for wet testing and verify flows, levels, and alarms under controlled conditions
Run process performance testing at design conditions and sample treated water quality
Train operators on the new train and confirm procedures and drawings reflect as built conditions
Accept the train into service with signed commissioning records and a remaining deficiency plan

tasks.explanation: Dry testing protects equipment before water is introduced, and performance testing protects the public. Acceptance without training and as built records leaves operations unsupported.

tasks.prompt: Order the performance acceptance sequence for a newly installed disinfection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: proving a new disinfection system meets its guaranteed performance before final payment.

cards.label: Agree the acceptance test protocol, test conditions, and pass criteria before testing begins
Calibrate all test instruments and confirm sampling locations and methods
Run the acceptance tests at the specified flows and water quality conditions
Compare results with the guaranteed values and document any shortfalls
Require correction and retesting for any failed criterion before acceptance is signed
Release final acceptance and warranty start only after all criteria pass and records are filed

tasks.explanation: Pass criteria agreed in advance prevent disputes after testing. Final payment follows demonstrated performance, not installation alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the handover sequence from a capital project team to operations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: transferring a completed upgrade into normal operational control.

cards.label: Confirm commissioning is complete and the asset performs to specification
Deliver as built drawings, manuals, warranties, and spare parts to the operations team
Complete operator training and competency checks on the new equipment
Transfer open deficiencies and warranty items to a tracked list with owners and dates
Update the asset register, maintenance plans, and the DWQMS operational plan
Hold a formal handover sign off with project, operations, and maintenance leads

tasks.explanation: Operations cannot own an asset it has not been trained on or given records for. Formal sign off makes the transfer of accountability explicit.

tasks.prompt: Order the multi year capital forecasting sequence for a water utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: building a ten year capital forecast from asset and growth evidence.

cards.label: Compile asset condition, remaining life, capacity, and growth demand information
List candidate projects with scope, timing drivers, and rough order costs
Rank projects by compliance risk, service risk, and consequence of deferral
Phase the ranked projects across the forecast years within funding capacity
Test the phased plan against rate and reserve impacts with finance staff
Present the forecast for owner approval and update it annually with new evidence

tasks.explanation: Ranking by risk must precede phasing by affordability, otherwise urgent compliance work can be displaced by easier projects. Annual updates keep the forecast honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the engineering consultant management sequence for a design assignment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: managing an external engineering firm from selection to delivered design.

cards.label: Define the assignment scope, deliverables, schedule, and fee structure in writing
Select the consultant through the procurement process and execute the agreement
Hold a kickoff meeting to confirm design basis, standards, and owner review points
Review progress at set milestones and provide timely owner decisions and information
Review deliverables for quality and completeness and require corrections where needed
Close the assignment with a performance evaluation filed for future selections

tasks.explanation: A clear scope and milestone reviews keep consultant work aligned with operations needs. The closing evaluation improves the next procurement.

tasks.prompt: Order the post project review sequence after a major capital project is completed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: structured lessons learned review within months of project completion.

cards.label: Gather final cost, schedule, scope change, and performance data for the project
Interview the project team, operations staff, and the contractor on what worked and what did not
Compare outcomes with the original business case and explain the major variances
Identify root causes of overruns, delays, or operational problems encountered
Issue recommendations and assign owners to update standards, templates, and specifications
Present the review to senior management and file it where future project teams can find it

tasks.explanation: Data and interviews come before conclusions. Recommendations only help if they are assigned and filed where the next project will actually look.

tasks.prompt: Order the launch sequence for a system wide optimization program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: utility wide program covering treatment, storage, and distribution performance.

cards.label: Establish baseline performance for water quality, energy, chemical use, and losses across the system
Select the priority optimization themes and define targets for each theme
Form theme teams with operators, maintenance, engineering, and water quality staff
Approve the program plan, resources, and reporting rhythm with senior management
Launch the first improvement projects and track them on a shared program dashboard
Review program progress quarterly and reallocate effort to the themes delivering results

tasks.explanation: Baselines and targets come before projects, otherwise improvement cannot be demonstrated. Quarterly review keeps the program focused on results rather than activity.

tasks.prompt: Order the whole plant mass balance review sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reconciling flows and solids across intake, treatment, residuals, and finished water.

cards.label: Define the balance boundary and the period to be reconciled, using a representative operating month
Collect metered flows, tank levels, residuals volumes, and chemical usage for the period
Check meters and records for gaps or suspect readings and correct the data set
Build the balance and quantify unaccounted flows and solids for each process area
Investigate the largest discrepancies for leaks, meter error, or unrecorded waste streams
Report the reconciled balance and assign actions to reduce unexplained losses

tasks.explanation: A balance built on unchecked meter data produces false conclusions. Data validation precedes calculation, and investigation follows the largest gaps.

tasks.prompt: Order the disinfection strategy optimization sequence at utility scale.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reviewing primary and secondary disinfection across plant and distribution system.

cards.label: Compile disinfection performance data including CT credits, residuals, and byproduct results
Confirm the required inactivation credits and residual targets for each barrier
Model options such as dose points, contact improvements, and booster locations using plant data
Trial the preferred option in one area with enhanced monitoring of residuals and byproducts
Evaluate trial results against water quality, compliance, and cost criteria
Adopt the strategy utility wide and update procedures, setpoints, and training

tasks.explanation: Credits and targets define the boundaries that optimization cannot cross. A monitored trial proves the option before it becomes the system standard.

tasks.prompt: Order the membrane fleet optimization sequence for a multi train plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: equalizing performance and life across all membrane trains in a large plant.

cards.label: Compile normalized permeability, cleaning history, and integrity results for every train
Rank trains by condition and identify the units limiting plant capacity or efficiency
Adjust rotation and cleaning schedules so duty is shared according to condition
Trial revised cleaning triggers on the worst performing train and measure recovery
Standardize the effective settings across the fleet and update the membrane management plan
Forecast module replacement needs and feed them into the capital plan

tasks.explanation: Fleet decisions need comparable normalized data for every train. Replacement forecasting connects daily optimization to long term capital planning.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet system fleet management sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: managing multiple UV reactors and banks as a single disinfection fleet.

cards.label: Inventory reactor capacity, lamp age, sleeve condition, and validated ranges for each unit
Confirm the duty and standby philosophy so required dose is met with one unit out of service
Set dose pacing and flow splitting rules that keep every duty reactor inside its validated range
Schedule lamp and sleeve work in a rolling plan that never removes too much capacity at once
Trend dose performance fleet wide and investigate reactors drifting from expected output
Review the fleet plan annually against flow growth and updated validation information

tasks.explanation: Dose compliance depends on the fleet, not a single reactor. Capacity planning must protect credited disinfection during maintenance, not only at peak flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the filter optimization program sequence at plant scale.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: coordinated optimization of all filters in a conventional treatment plant.

cards.label: Establish baseline run times, headloss development, and effluent turbidity for every filter
Standardize backwash criteria and sequences so filters are compared on the same basis
Identify the filters with the shortest runs or highest turbidity and investigate their media and underdrains
Trial rate and coagulation adjustments on one filter while holding the others as controls
Adopt proven settings plant wide and update filter operating procedures
Track run length, water used in backwash, and turbidity in monthly performance reports

tasks.explanation: Common backwash criteria make filter comparison meaningful. Plant wide adoption follows a controlled trial, and monthly tracking shows whether gains persist.

tasks.prompt: Order the residuals management optimization sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reducing residuals volume and handling cost without harming treated water quality.

cards.label: Measure residuals volumes, solids concentrations, and disposal costs for each source stream
Review thickening and dewatering performance and identify where water content can be reduced
Trial operational changes such as revised sludge withdrawal timing on one stream
Confirm treated water quality and clarifier performance are unaffected during the trial
Calculate the verified reduction in volume and disposal cost against the baseline
Implement the proven changes and update the residuals management procedure

tasks.explanation: Volume and cost baselines come first so savings can be verified. Treated water quality is checked during the trial because residuals changes can upset the main process.

tasks.prompt: Order the process control strategy review sequence for plant automation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior review of automatic control loops, alarms, and SCADA setpoints.

cards.label: Inventory critical control loops, alarm setpoints, and manual overrides currently in use
Review alarm history to find nuisance alarms and alarms operators routinely ignore
Verify each critical loop still matches the process intent and the operating procedure
Rationalize the alarm list, correcting setpoints and removing duplicate or stale alarms
Test revised loops and alarms under supervision before leaving them in automatic control
Document the control strategy and schedule its review at a fixed interval

tasks.explanation: An alarm operators ignore provides no protection. Rationalization and supervised testing restore the control system as a real safeguard.

tasks.prompt: Order the water quality optimization sequence at the treatment and distribution interface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aligning plant finished water targets with distribution system water quality.

cards.label: Compile finished water and distribution results for residuals, turbidity, and disinfection byproducts
Identify where distribution quality degrades, such as long detention storage or dead ends
Review plant targets for residual, pH, and alkalinity against distribution performance
Trial adjusted plant targets with enhanced distribution monitoring at sentinel sites
Evaluate whether distribution quality improved without creating plant compliance risk
Set the agreed targets in both plant and distribution operating procedures

tasks.explanation: The plant cannot optimize in isolation from the system it supplies. Sentinel monitoring proves whether a plant change actually improves water at the tap.

tasks.prompt: Order the seasonal operations strategy sequence for spring runoff conditions.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the plant for high turbidity and cold water runoff each spring.

cards.label: Review previous runoff seasons for raw water peaks, chemical use, and process problems
Confirm chemical inventories, residuals capacity, and staffing plans for the runoff window
Update dose guidance, jar test frequency, and filter management rules for runoff conditions
Brief all shifts on the runoff plan, trigger levels, and escalation contacts
Operate to the plan during runoff with daily senior review of raw and treated quality
Debrief after the season and revise the strategy with the lessons learned

tasks.explanation: Last season evidence shapes this season plan. A debrief converts one difficult season into preparation for the next.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual emergency management program cycle for a water utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one year of emergency preparedness from plan review to exercised readiness.

cards.label: Review the emergency plan against organizational changes, new hazards, and lessons from incidents
Update contact lists, mutual aid agreements, and resource inventories in the plan
Train staff on their emergency roles and confirm new staff complete orientation
Conduct at least one exercise that tests notification, decision making, and field response
Evaluate exercise performance and record gaps as corrective actions with due dates
Report program status and readiness to senior management and the owner

tasks.explanation: A plan that is never trained or exercised is only a document. The cycle ends with corrective actions and a readiness report, not with the exercise itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the incident command leadership sequence for a suspected contamination event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior leadership response from first credible report to controlled investigation.

cards.label: Receive the report, verify its source, and appoint an incident lead with clear authority
Protect public health first by isolating suspect water and increasing disinfection and sampling
Notify the overall responsible operator, senior management, and regulatory contacts as required
Establish an incident team with operations, water quality, communications, and logistics roles
Direct the investigation sampling plan and hold points for any return to normal service
Stand down in stages only when results confirm the water is safe, and document every decision

tasks.explanation: Isolation and notification precede investigation conclusions. Return to service requires confirming results, and the decision record protects both the public and the utility.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership response sequence for a loss of disinfection event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant wide response when primary disinfection is lost during production.

cards.label: Confirm the failure, stop or divert affected flow, and prevent inadequately disinfected water reaching storage
Notify the overall responsible operator and make the adverse water quality notifications required by regulation
Restore disinfection using backup equipment or an approved alternate method
Verify disinfection credit and treated water quality before releasing water to the system
Increase monitoring in storage and distribution until normal conditions are proven stable
Complete the incident report, root cause review, and any required corrective actions

tasks.explanation: Stopping affected water comes before restoring equipment. Regulatory notification and verified quality are conditions for return to normal service.

tasks.prompt: Order the flood response leadership sequence for a treatment plant in a flood risk area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: from flood warning to post flood recovery of plant operations.

cards.label: Monitor forecasts and river levels and activate the flood plan at the defined trigger
Protect chemicals, electrical equipment, records, and portable equipment before water arrives
Adjust operations, secure the site, and evacuate non essential staff if conditions require it
Maintain essential treatment and monitoring with safe staffing during the event
Inspect for damage, contamination, and electrical safety before restarting affected systems
Restore full service in stages, verify water quality, and document the event and lessons

tasks.explanation: Triggers activate the plan before water arrives, when protection is still possible. Restart follows inspection and verification, not the receding water alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the power failure leadership sequence for an extended outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: utility leadership during a multi hour loss of normal power supply.

cards.label: Confirm the outage scope and expected duration with the electricity provider
Verify generators have started, fuel levels are adequate, and critical loads are powered
Prioritize treatment, disinfection, pumping, and monitoring loads within generator capacity
Arrange fuel resupply, staff rotations, and relief for critical roles for the outage duration
Monitor treated water storage and communicate conservation needs if supply becomes limited
Restore normal power in stages, verify all systems, and review generator performance after the event

tasks.explanation: Generator capacity forces explicit priorities. Fuel, staffing, and storage management determine whether the utility outlasts a long outage.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical spill leadership response sequence at a treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior response to a significant treatment chemical spill on site.

cards.label: Ensure people are safe, evacuate the affected area, and account for all staff and visitors
Identify the chemical and quantity from a safe location and activate spill response resources
Stop the source if it can be done safely and contain the spill to protect drains and watercourses
Make the required notifications to emergency services, regulators, and senior management
Direct cleanup by trained responders with correct protective equipment and disposal arrangements
Investigate the cause, restore the area, and complete corrective actions before normal use resumes

tasks.explanation: People come before property and cleanup. Notifications and cause investigation are part of the response, not paperwork after it.

tasks.prompt: Order the cyber incident response sequence for a SCADA system compromise.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: leadership response when control system integrity is in doubt.

cards.label: Confirm the anomaly, preserve evidence, and notify senior management and information technology support
Isolate affected control networks and switch critical processes to safe manual operation
Verify treatment, disinfection, and monitoring are being controlled and recorded manually
Engage qualified specialists to assess the compromise and advise on recovery
Restore systems in stages from known good backups with enhanced monitoring
Review the incident, strengthen access controls and backups, and brief staff on lessons learned

tasks.explanation: Manual safe operation protects water quality while specialists work. Restoration from known good backups, in stages, prevents reinfection of the control system.

tasks.prompt: Order the mutual aid activation sequence when an emergency exceeds local resources.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: requesting and integrating help from neighbouring utilities during a major event.

cards.label: Confirm local resources are insufficient and define exactly what help is needed
Contact the mutual aid partners and the provincial coordination channels with the specific request
Agree the scope, supervision, safety requirements, and cost arrangements before crews deploy
Receive incoming crews with a safety briefing, site orientation, and assigned work packages
Integrate mutual aid crews into the incident structure and track their work and hours
Release crews when no longer needed, thank partners formally, and settle costs as agreed

tasks.explanation: A specific request gets useful help faster than a general appeal. Incoming crews work safely only when they are briefed and integrated, not simply present.

tasks.prompt: Order the emergency exercise design and delivery sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario Class 4 water treatment system used for study. All sequences follow standard practice in the cited sources for Ontario drinking water operations under Ontario Regulation 170/03 and the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: designing a realistic exercise that tests the emergency plan and its people.

cards.label: Set exercise objectives tied to the highest risks and the weakest areas from past incidents
Design a scenario with timed injects that force decisions, notifications, and field actions
Brief controllers and evaluators while keeping the scenario confidential from participants
Deliver the exercise and record decisions, times, and communications as they occur
Hold a hot debrief immediately after, then a structured evaluation against the objectives
Convert evaluation findings into corrective actions in the emergency program tracker

tasks.explanation: Objectives tied to real weaknesses make the exercise worth its cost. Findings that never become tracked actions waste the learning.
